1	# Fizeau
2	
3	Embeddable Go agent runtime - local-model-first via LM Studio.
4	
5	[![CI](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
6	[![Release](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest)
7	[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
8	
9	Fizeau is a Go library that implements a coding agent runtime - a tool-calling
10	LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
11	structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
12	[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
13	Prioritizes local model inference via LM Studio and Ollama, with transparent
14	escalation to cloud providers.
15	
16	## Install
17	
18	```bash
19	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/master/install.sh | bash
20	```
21	
22	Or with Go:
23	
24	```bash
25	go install github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/cmd/fiz@latest
26	```
27	
28	## Quick Start
29	
30	Start [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) with a model that supports tool
31	calling (Qwen 3.5+, Llama 3.2+), then:
32	
33	```bash
34	fiz -p "Read main.go and tell me the package name"
35	```
36	
37	Fizeau connects to `localhost:1234` by default.
38	
39	### With Anthropic
40	
41	```bash
42	export FIZEAU_PROVIDER=anthropic
43	export FIZEAU_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
44	export FIZEAU_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-20250514
45	fiz -p "Read main.go and tell me the package name"
46	```
47	
48	## Demos
49	
50	### Read a file and explain it
51	
52	[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/placeholder.svg)](website/static/demos/file-read.cast)
53	
54	```
55	$ fiz -p 'Read main.go and explain what this program does'
56	
57	This program is a simple HTTP server that listens on port 8080 and responds
58	with "Hello from Fizeau!" to any request.
59	[success] tokens: 1861 in / 70 out
60	```
61	
62	### Edit a config file
63	
64	```
65	$ fiz -p 'Read config.yaml, change the server port from 8080 to 9090, then verify'
66	
67	Done. The server port in config.yaml has been changed from 8080 to 9090.
68	[success] tokens: 4082 in / 127 out
69	```
70	
71	### Explore project structure
72	
73	```
74	$ fiz -p 'List all Go files and summarize the package structure'
75	
76	Package Structure:
77	├── cmd/server/main.go       (package main)
78	├── internal/api/handler.go  (package api)
79	├── internal/api/middleware.go (package api)
80	└── internal/db/postgres.go  (package db)
81	
82	A typical Go project with cmd/ for entry points, internal/ for private packages.
83	[success] tokens: 6388 in / 297 out
84	```
85	
86	## As a Library
87	
88	```go
89	import (
90	    "context"
91	    "fmt"
92	
93	    "github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau"
94	    _ "github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/configinit"
95	)
96	
97	func main() {
98	    svc, err := fizeau.New(fizeau.ServiceOptions{})
99	    if err != nil {
100	        panic(err)
101	    }
102	    events, err := svc.Execute(context.Background(), fizeau.ServiceExecuteRequest{
103	        Prompt:   "Read main.go and tell me the package name",
104	        ModelRef: "cheap",
105	        WorkDir:  ".",
106	    })
107	    if err != nil {
108	        panic(err)
109	    }
110	    for event := range events {
111	        fmt.Println(event.Type)
112	    }
113	}
114	```
115	
116	## Features
117	
118	- **Embeddable library** — `fizeau.New(...).Execute(ctx, request)`, no subprocess overhead
119	- **Local-model-first** — LM Studio, Ollama via OpenAI-compatible API
120	- **Multi-provider** — OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Claude, virtual (test replay)
121	- **9 built-in tools** — read, write, edit, bash, find, grep, ls, patch, task
122	- **Session logging** — JSONL with replay and cost tracking
123	- **System prompt composition** — pi-style builder with context file discovery
124	- **Standalone CLI** — `fiz -p "prompt"` with config, logging, replay
125	
126	## Configuration
127	
128	```yaml
129	# .fizeau/config.yaml
130	providers:
131	  local:
132	    type: lmstudio
133	    base_url: http://localhost:1234/v1
134	    model: qwen3.5-7b
135	default: local
136	preset: default                  # system prompt style (see below)
137	max_iterations: 20
138	session_log_dir: .fizeau/sessions
139	tools:
140	  bash:
141	    output_filter:
142	      mode: off                  # off | rtk | auto
143	      rtk_binary: rtk
144	      max_bytes: 51200
145	```
146	
147	Environment overrides: `FIZEAU_PROVIDER`, `FIZEAU_BASE_URL`, `FIZEAU_API_KEY`, `FIZEAU_MODEL`
148	
149	`tools.bash.output_filter.mode: rtk` proxies allowlisted noisy commands such as
150	`git status` and `go test` through an installed `rtk` binary. If `rtk` is not
151	available, bash runs the original command and includes a fallback marker.
152	Built-in `read`, `find`, `grep`, and `ls` are not filtered.
153	
154	## System Prompt Presets
155	
156	Fizeau ships built-in system prompt presets that describe prompt intent.
157	Select one with `--preset` or the
158	top-level `preset` config field:
159	
160	| Preset      | Description                                           |
161	|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
162	| `default`   | Balanced, tool-aware prompt                          |
163	| `smart`     | Rich, thorough prompt for quality-sensitive runs      |
164	| `cheap`     | Pragmatic, direct prompt for latency/cost-sensitive runs |
165	| `minimal`   | Bare minimum — one sentence                           |
166	| `benchmark` | Non-interactive prompt optimized for evaluation       |
167	
168	When no preset is specified, `default` is used.
169	
170	## Session Replay
171	
172	Every run is logged. Replay past sessions:
173	
174	```bash
175	fiz log                  # list sessions
176	fiz replay <session-id>  # human-readable replay
177	```
178	
179	## Documentation
180	
181	- [Getting Started](https://documentdrivendx.github.io/fizeau/docs/getting-started/)
182	- [Routing Reference](docs/routing/index.md)
183	- [Microsite](https://documentdrivendx.github.io/fizeau/)
184	
185	## Contributing
186	
187	See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
188	
189	## License
190	
191	[MIT](LICENSE)
192

1	# ddx-agent-bench
2	
3	This directory contains the benchmark corpus and (gitignored) results for
4	`ddx-agent-bench`.
5	
6	## Layout
7	
8	```
9	bench/
10	  corpus/          # versioned task definitions (YAML/JSON)
11	  results/         # gitignored; populated by `ddx-agent-bench run`
12	```
13	
14	## Corpus format
15	
16	Each file in `bench/corpus/` is a YAML (or JSON) task:
17	
18	```yaml
19	id: unique-task-id
20	description: "Human-readable description"
21	prompt: |
22	  The prompt sent to the agent.
23	expected_tools:        # optional; informational only
24	  - read
25	  - find
26	permissions: safe      # safe | supervised | unrestricted
27	reasoning: low         # off | low | medium | high | xhigh | max | numeric tokens
28	tags:
29	  - tool-use
30	```
31	
32	## Usage
33	
34	```sh
35	# List discovered candidates
36	ddx-agent-bench discover
37	
38	# Run corpus against all candidates
39	ddx-agent-bench run
40	
41	# Run against a specific harness only
42	ddx-agent-bench run --harness=claude
43	
44	# Render the most recent result
45	ddx-agent-bench report
46	ddx-agent-bench report --format=markdown
47	```
48	
49	Results are written to `bench/results/` and are **not tracked by git**.

1	# DDX Agent Benchmark Scripts
2	
3	This directory contains scripts and config for running ddx-agent under
4	Terminal-Bench/Harbor and capturing reproducible benchmark baselines.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	```bash
11	# Terminal-Bench dataset
12	harbor dataset pull terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2
13	
14	# Docker (local runtime)
15	docker info  # must succeed
16	```
17	
18	If `harbor` is not already installed, `smoke_run.sh` and `run_benchmark.sh`
19	now install it automatically with `uv tool install harbor`.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Smoke Run (adapter validation)
24	
25	Validates the Harbor adapter works end-to-end on a single task (~2 min).
26	
27	```bash
28	# With Anthropic API key
29	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/smoke_run.sh
30	
31	# With OpenRouter
32	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... ./scripts/benchmark/smoke_run.sh
33	```
34	
35	**Passing criterion**:
36	- ddx-agent exits 0
37	- `trajectory.json` is valid JSON with ≥ 1 step
38	- `reward.txt` exists (0 or 1 — both valid for smoke)
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Full Benchmark Run (baseline capture)
43	
44	Runs the committed 15-task subset and emits a machine-readable report.
45	
46	```bash
47	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
48	```
49	
50	The report is written to `benchmark-results/report-<TIMESTAMP>.json` and
51	contains git SHA, agent version, model, provider, per-task outcomes, and
52	the aggregate resolved-task rate.
53	
54	### Commit-independent runs
55	
56	You can point the same harness at a prebuilt ddx-agent binary instead of
57	rebuilding the current checkout:
58	
59	```bash
60	FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY=/path/to/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 \
61	FIZEAU_BENCH_SHA=<commit-under-test> \
62	./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
63	```
64	
65	This is the required path for evidence-grade before/after comparison across
66	multiple agent SHAs.
67	
68	### Dry-run harness validation
69	
70	Use dry-run mode to validate the staged binary/config and recorded metadata
71	without invoking Harbor:
72	
73	```bash
74	DDX_BENCH_DRY_RUN=1 \
75	FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY=/path/to/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 \
76	DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_MODEL=qwen/qwen3.6-plus \
77	./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
78	```
79	
80	### Comparing two baselines
81	
82	```bash
83	# Capture baseline before a change
84	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
85	# ... make changes ...
86	# Capture new run
87	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
88	
89	# Compare (jq example)
90	jq '{resolved_rate: .summary.resolved_task_rate, tasks: [.tasks[] | {id, outcome}]}' \
91	  benchmark-results/report-*.json
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Task Subset
97	
98	The evidence-grade 15-task benchmark subset is defined in `task-subset-v2.yaml`.
99	`task-subset-v1.yaml` remains in the repo as the historical placeholder manifest
100	from the original benchmark design and should not be used for before/after claims.
101	**Do not modify task IDs without updating the version field and filing a bead.**
102	
103	Subset version policy: see SD-009 §3.
104	
105	## Evidence-Grade Comparison Config
106	
107	The pinned comparison controls live in `evidence-grade-comparison.env`. That file
108	freezes the intended `before` and `after` SHAs for the original benchmark-change
109	window plus the shared dataset, subset, runtime, preset, and provider/model route.
110	The only per-run inputs that should change are:
111	
112	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY`
113	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_SHA` (set to either `DDX_BENCH_BEFORE_SHA` or `DDX_BENCH_AFTER_SHA`)
114	
115	---
116	
117	## Harbor Adapter
118	
119	`harbor_agent.py` is the `BaseInstalledAgent` Python adapter that Harbor uses
120	to install and run ddx-agent inside each task container. It handles:
121	
122	1. **`install()`** — copies the `linux/amd64` binary and writes a provider config
123	2. **`run()`** — invokes `ddx-agent --json --preset benchmark -p "<task>"`
124	3. **`populate_context_post_run()`** — converts session JSONL to ATIF v1.4 trajectory
125	
126	The adapter's provider and prompt behavior are controlled by benchmark env vars
127	supplied by the runner, including:
128	
129	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_NAME`
130	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_TYPE`
131	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_MODEL`
132	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`
133	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV`
134	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_HEADERS_JSON`
135	- `DDX_BENCH_PRESET`
136	- `DDX_BENCH_SYSTEM_APPEND`
137	
138	**Build the linux/amd64 binary before running**:
139	
140	```bash
141	GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o scripts/benchmark/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 ./cmd/fiz
142	```
143	
144	### Credential injection
145	
146	The adapter passes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the host
147	into the container via `get_env()`. A minimal config file is written during
148	`install()` that references `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}` — ddx-agent's config loader
149	expands env vars at load time.
150	
151	If the expected key env var is unset, the benchmark scripts now fall back to the
152	matching provider entry in the host ddx-agent config (`.agent/config.yaml` or
153	`~/.config/agent/config.yaml`) and export the discovered `api_key` before
154	invoking Harbor.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## Thresholds (from SD-009 §5)
159	
160	| Metric | Regression floor | Aspirational |
161	|--------|-----------------|-------------|
162	| Resolved-task rate | ≥ 55% | ≥ 70% |
163	| Clarification-question rate | < 10% | < 5% |
164	| Shell anti-pattern rate | < 30% of bash calls | < 10% |
165	| Structured-edit success rate | ≥ 70% | ≥ 90% |
166	
167	---
168	
169	## References
170	
171	- `SD-008-terminal-bench-integration.md` — Harbor/Terminal-Bench integration audit
172	- `SD-009-benchmark-mode.md` — Benchmark mode, metrics, thresholds
173	- `benchmark-baseline-2026-04-08.md` — Initial baseline characterization
174

1	# Beadbench
2	
3	Beadbench compares DDx `execute-bead` performance across harness/model arms on
4	frozen historical beads. It is separate from the Terminal-Bench runner under
5	`scripts/benchmark/`.
6	
7	## What It Measures
8	
9	Each task pins:
10	
11	- a local project root
12	- a bead id
13	- the base revision before the known successful implementation
14	- the known-good revision
15	- a verifier command
16	
17	The runner clones the source project into a disposable sandbox, reopens the
18	historical bead inside that sandbox, commits the tracker-only reopen, and runs:
19	
20	```bash
21	ddx agent execute-bead <bead-id> --from <base-rev> --no-merge --json ...
22	```
23	
24	The source repository and source tracker are never mutated.
25	
26	## Preflight
27	
28	Before any real dispatch the runner validates the environment and the
29	selected tasks. Run preflight in isolation with:
30	
31	```bash
32	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py --preflight
33	```
34	
35	Preflight checks:
36	
37	- `ddx agent execute-bead --help` advertises every flag beadbench sends
38	  (`--from`, `--no-merge`, `--json`, `--project`, `--harness`,
39	  `--provider`, `--model`, `--model-ref`, `--effort`, `--context-budget`).
40	- Each selected task's `project_root` is an existing git repository.
41	- Each task's `base_rev` and `known_good_rev` resolve to commits in that
42	  repository.
43	- Each task's `bead_id` is known to `ddx bead show` from within
44	  `project_root`.
45	
46	A full run performs preflight automatically and refuses to dispatch when
47	any check fails. Use `--skip-preflight` to bypass (for offline debugging
48	only). Preflight output is written to `<run-dir>/preflight.json`.
49	
50	## Smoke
51	
52	Validate command generation without invoking any agents:
53	
54	```bash
55	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py --dry-run --limit-tasks 2 --limit-arms 2
56	```
57	
58	Run a narrow real baseline:
59	
60	```bash
61	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py \
62	  --task helix-build-selector-readiness \
63	  --arm codex-gpt54 \
64	  --timeout-seconds 1800
65	```
66	
67	Slice the expanded matrix before launching expensive runs:
68	
69	```bash
70	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py --dry-run \
71	  --tier smoke --arm-tier core
72	
73	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py --dry-run \
74	  --project axon --difficulty medium --arm claude-sonnet46
75	
76	python3 scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py --dry-run \
77	  --category rust-auth --arm-tier frontier
78	```
79	
80	Results are written to `benchmark-results/beadbench/run-<timestamp>-<pid>/report.json`.
81	
82	## Timeout evidence
83	
84	When `--timeout-seconds` trips before `execute-bead` returns, the runner still
85	records what it has:
86	
87	- `stdout.txt` / `stderr.txt` hold the partial streams captured before the
88	  child was killed.
89	- `execute-result.json` is written whenever the trailing stdout contained a
90	  recoverable JSON object; its `preserve_rev`/`result_rev` (if any) is lifted
91	  into `result.timeout.preserve_rev`.
92	- `timeout-sandbox-state.json` records the sandbox HEAD, commits ahead of
93	  `base_rev`, `git status --short`, tracked diff names, and any
94	  `refs/execute-bead/preserve/*` refs left behind.
95	- `result.timeout.progress_class` buckets the run as `no_output`,
96	  `read_only_progress`, or `write_progress` so slow-but-healthy local-model
97	  runs can be told apart from stuck reasoning loops.
98	
99	Execute-phase and verifier-phase timeouts are recorded separately and do
100	not overwrite each other:
101	
102	- An execute-phase timeout sets `result.status=timeout`,
103	  `result.phases.execute.status=timeout`, and leaves
104	  `result.phases.verify.status=skipped`.
105	- A verifier-phase timeout keeps the execute status intact
106	  (`result.phases.execute.status=success`) and records
107	  `result.verify.status=timeout` /
108	  `result.phases.verify.status=timeout` with its own `duration_ms` and
109	  `timeout_seconds`. Verifier timeouts appear in the summary under
110	  `verified_timeout` rather than being counted as executable pass/fail.
111	
112	Reports include per-arm `executable` counts (runs where the verifier
113	actually produced pass/fail) and `verified_pass_rate` computed over those
114	executable runs only, so dry-runs and unreachable verifiers do not dilute
115	the signal.
116	
117	Fixture coverage lives in `scripts/beadbench/test_run_beadbench.py`
118	(`python3 scripts/beadbench/test_run_beadbench.py`).
119	
120	Probe model-side reasoning controls before local-model evidence runs:
121	
122	```bash
123	python3 scripts/beadbench/probe_reasoning_controls.py \
124	  --arm agent-vidar-omlx-qwen36-27b
125	```
126	
127	The probe records whether each provider accepts the control field, separates
128	`reasoning_content`, and visibly suppresses thinking when reasoning is turned
129	off. Results are written to
130	`benchmark-results/beadbench/reasoning-probe-*.json`.
131	
132	Each probe emits one progress line as soon as it returns, flushed
133	immediately, so a slow local arm can be distinguished from a stuck run
134	without waiting for the full arm to finish. For a quick local diagnostic
135	that only exercises the two Qwen controls most likely to drive reasoning
136	loops, pass `--probe` once per probe id:
137	
138	```bash
139	python3 scripts/beadbench/probe_reasoning_controls.py \
140	  --arm agent-vidar-omlx-qwen36-27b \
141	  --probe qwen_off --probe qwen_budget_32
142	```
143	
144	The selected probe ids are recorded under `probe_filter` in the generated
145	report JSON.
146	
147	For LM Studio specifically, the probe now tests two distinct API surfaces:
148	
149	- OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, which is the execute-bead surface
150	  because it supports custom tools, but where Qwen/GPT-OSS reasoning controls
151	  may be accepted without being honored by the loaded template.
152	- Native `/api/v1/chat`, which exposes LM Studio's documented
153	  `reasoning: off|low|medium|high|on` control and returns
154	  `stats.reasoning_output_tokens`, but is not currently the execute-bead
155	  surface because LM Studio documents custom tools on `/v1/chat/completions`
156	  and `/v1/responses`, not native chat.
157	
158	The LM Studio native probes are
159	`lmstudio_native_reasoning_off`, `lmstudio_native_reasoning_low`, and
160	`lmstudio_native_reasoning_high`. Treat a `recommended_wire_format` of
161	`lmstudio_native` as evidence that LM Studio can control reasoning on the
162	native endpoint, not as proof that the current agent tool loop can switch to
163	that endpoint without a separate tools-compatible design.
164	
165	Probe runs are classification-only, not evidence-grade benchmark results. A
166	single probe tells us whether a request shape appears to be honored on one
167	provider/model surface; it does not promote an arm into the separability
168	leaderboard by itself. Evidence-grade arms still follow the three-run rule
169	described below.
170	
171	Current local evidence: on 2026-04-23, Vidar OMLX
172	`Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit` and `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit` accepted both the legacy
173	`thinking` map and Qwen controls, but only Qwen
174	`enable_thinking`/`thinking_budget` changed observable behavior. `qwen_off`
175	returned a short direct answer while the no-control and `thinking`-map probes
176	filled the response with visible thinking text.
177	
178	### Vidar OMLX `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8` reasoning control: unsupported/unknown
179	
180	The same probe run found that Vidar OMLX `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8` emits
181	`reasoning_content` by default but has no known budget/off control in this
182	matrix. A 2026-04-23 live probe of the no-control arm
183	(`benchmark-results/beadbench/reasoning-probe-20260423T034159Z.json`) returned
184	HTTP 200 with `content_chars=0, reasoning_chars=88` at `max_tokens=48` and
185	`recommended_wire_format=unknown`: the assistant message carried only
186	`reasoning_content`, all completion tokens were consumed by reasoning, and no
187	visible answer remained under the budget.
188	
189	Wire-format rationale:
190	
191	- GPT-OSS is a Harmony-format model family (OpenAI `gpt-oss-20b`/`gpt-oss-120b`).
192	  Harmony expects a top-level `reasoning_effort` ∈ {`low`,`medium`,`high`} and
193	  does not accept Qwen's `enable_thinking` / `thinking_budget`, nor
194	  Anthropic-style `thinking: {type, budget_tokens}`.
195	- The OMLX provider is pinned to `ThinkingWireFormatQwen` with
196	  `StrictThinkingModelMatch=true`, so the native agent rejects any explicit
197	  reasoning request against `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-Q8` at serialization time rather
198	  than silently sending Qwen fields the template would ignore. This is enforced
199	  by `TestQwenReasoningSerializationRejectsNonQwenModels` in
200	  `internal/provider/openai/openai_test.go`; the arm-level manifest rationale
201	  therefore omits `effort` and does not attempt `ReasoningOff`.
202	- No GPT-OSS-specific wire format is wired into the provider because the probe
203	  has not yet confirmed that any effort-level knob measurably changes reasoning
204	  output on this OMLX build. Until a live probe reports
205	  `recommended_wire_format=gpt_oss_effort`, the arm is treated as
206	  `reasoning-control=unsupported/unknown`.
207	
208	How to interpret benchmark failures on `agent-vidar-omlx-gptoss20b`:
209	
210	- Treat an empty `content` with non-empty `reasoning_content` as the expected
211	  baseline, not a harness bug. The model answered in reasoning; the answer did
212	  not fit under the caller's `max_tokens` budget.
213	- Prefer evidence-grade arms with a verified reasoning control
214	  (`agent-vidar-omlx-qwen36-27b`, `agent-vidar-omlx-qwen36-35b`) when comparing
215	  local models against frontier baselines. The GPT-OSS arm is a research arm
216	  for non-Qwen OMLX behavior, not a substitute for a budgeted local-model arm.
217	- Extending the `probe_reasoning_controls.py` PROBES list with
218	  `gptoss_effort_{low,medium,high}` and `gptoss_reasoning_map_low` lets a
219	  future live run classify the model as `gpt_oss_effort` (honored),
220	  `gpt_oss_unsupported` (accepted but no behavioral change), or `unknown`
221	  (request rejected). Promote the arm to `reasoning-control=supported` only
222	  after a recorded probe reports `gptoss_effort_changes_reasoning=true`.
223	
224	### Bragi LM Studio `qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b` reasoning control: operational blocker
225	
226	A later live investigation (2026-04-23) against Bragi LM Studio on port 1234
227	showed the earlier "all timeouts" finding was an artifact of the probe's
228	45-second cap, not a server refusal. Raising the probe timeout to 120 seconds
229	makes every tested control shape return HTTP 200, including no control,
230	`thinking` map (both `budget_tokens=32` and `=0`), Qwen `enable_thinking=false
231	thinking_budget=0`, Qwen `enable_thinking=true thinking_budget=32`,
232	`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`, OpenAI-style
233	`reasoning_effort=minimal`, and the `/no_think` prompt convention. In every
234	response the assistant message contains empty `content` and a populated
235	`reasoning_content`, and `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`
236	equals the emitted completion tokens.
237	
238	Server/version evidence (from `GET /api/v0/models/qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b`):
239	
240	| field | value |
241	| --- | --- |
242	| `arch` | `qwen35moe` |
243	| `publisher` | `qwen` |
244	| `compatibility_type` | `gguf` |
245	| `quantization` | `Q4_K_M` |
246	| `state` | `loaded` |
247	| `max_context_length` | 262144 |
248	| `loaded_context_length` | 262144 |
249	| `capabilities` | `["tool_use"]` (no `"thinking"` / no reasoning budget capability) |
250	
251	LM Studio HTTP response header reports `X-Powered-By: Express`; the model is
252	a vision-language GGUF served from `qwen35moe` at Q4_K_M.
253	
254	Conclusion: the LM Studio build accepts every known reasoning-control wire
255	shape but does not forward any of them into this GGUF's chat template, so
256	reasoning is produced unconditionally and cannot be bounded from the
257	request. This is a model/template limitation, not a Qwen-family wire-format
258	bug — the Qwen controls are the correct per-family shape and are used for
259	LM Studio Qwen models regardless, so that `ReasoningOff` emits the intended
260	`enable_thinking=false, thinking_budget=0` disable signal for any LM Studio
261	Qwen build that does respect it. Classify LM Studio reasoning behavior per
262	loaded model/template, not per engine: Bragi `qwen/qwen3.6-35b-a3b` is
263	currently a no-budget arm, but a different LM Studio-served Qwen model may
264	still honor the same request shape and must be re-probed before routing relies
265	on its `effort` label. For the current Bragi model, reasoning-control probes
266	are expected to be `accepted=true` but behaviorally no-op, and the beadbench
267	tracker's `effort` label does not change observable runtime reasoning. Use
268	OMLX `Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit` / `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit` when enforced reasoning
269	budgets are needed.
270	
271	## Tasks invalid for model-comparison scoring
272	
273	A task may carry `"model_comparison_valid": false` in `manifest-v1.json` when its
274	verifier is known to produce model-independent results (for example, the verifier
275	fixture is internally inconsistent, the acceptance command has a defect, or the
276	upstream project's state diverges from the pinned base revision). Such tasks
277	should be excluded from separability aggregates and leaderboard-style rollups;
278	the runner still executes them so harness-side regressions remain visible.
279	
280	The flag is wired through `run_beadbench.py`: each result echoes
281	`model_comparison_valid`, and `summarize()` emits a `model_comparison` block
282	(alongside the top-level totals) that excludes flagged tasks and records the
283	`excluded_task_ids`. `print_summary` prints the separability pass rate and the
284	excluded ids on every run. Top-level counts still include every run so harness
285	regressions on flagged tasks remain visible.
286	
287	Currently marked invalid:
288	
289	- `helix-triage-blanket-priming` — the helix `tests/validate-skills.sh`
290	  mixed-ready-semantics block diffs `ddx bead ready --execution --json` against
291	  `validate_execution_ready_beads.execution_ready_beads` on a shared fixture; the
292	  two views disagree (`hx-in-progress-build` vs `hx-ready-epic`) regardless of
293	  what the agent edits, so both Codex and Sonnet execute-success runs fail the
294	  verifier identically (see
295	  `benchmark-results/beadbench/run-20260423T054306Z-3937255/report.json`). The
296	  task can be re-enabled once helix reconciles the CLI and validator views of
297	  the execution-ready surface.
298	
299	  Under the `model_comparison` aggregate, both the Codex GPT-5.4 and Sonnet 4.6
300	  runs for this task id are dropped from separability totals — they currently
301	  appear only in the top-level executable/verified counts as harness evidence.
302	  The upstream fixture fix (reconciling `ddx bead ready --execution --json` with
303	  `validate_execution_ready_beads.execution_ready_beads`, or rewriting the
304	  expected-ids list to
305	  `['hx-in-progress-build', 'hx-ready-build', 'hx-ready-review', 'hx-ready-vague']`)
306	  lives in the helix repository and is intentionally deferred out of this bead's
307	  scope; flipping `model_comparison_valid` back to `true` is the re-enable step
308	  once that change lands.
309	
310	## Evidence Rules
311	
312	- Evidence-grade claims require at least three repetitions per task/arm.
313	- Single-run results are diagnostic only.
314	- Reasoning-control probes are capability classification, not a substitute for
315	  the three-run evidence-grade rule.
316	- Provider and harness infrastructure failures are reported separately from
317	  verifier failures.
318	- Reasoning control is part of the capability matrix: each local-model arm must
319	  declare an effort and have probe evidence for the wire format that enforces it.
320	- Changing `manifest-v1.json` task ids, base revisions, or verifier commands
321	  creates a new benchmark version.
322	- Use `tier=smoke` tasks for fast harness sanity checks, `tier=core` for the
323	  regular comparison set, `tier=extended` for hard/expensive complexity labels,
324	  and `tier=expensive` only when the required external environment is ready.
325	
326	## Initial Arms
327	
328	The manifest includes the requested comparison shape plus controls:
329	
330	- embedded/native agent via OpenRouter GPT-5.4
331	- Codex GPT-5.4
332	- Pi with Qwen 3.6 27B-class pin
333	- native agent pinned to Vidar OMLX Qwen 3.6 on port 1235
334	- native agent pinned to Bragi LM Studio Qwen 3.6 on port 1234
335	- lower-effort local Qwen arms for reasoning-budget sensitivity
336	- Sonnet and Opus arms for hard-task separability
337	- GPT-5.4 Mini, Gemini Flash, and OpenRouter Haiku cost controls
338	- Vidar OMLX GPT-OSS 20B without Qwen reasoning controls as a non-Qwen local
339	  model research arm
340	
341	Validate exact model strings with `ddx agent capabilities <harness>` before
342	evidence-grade runs.
343

1	# Matrix Cost Guards
2	
3	This directory records the Step 5 procedure for deriving SD-010 matrix cost
4	caps from observation rather than from a formula guessed before a run.
5	
6	## Procedure
7	
8	1. Use the current anchor profile and the canary task expected to burn the most
9	   tokens:
10	
11	   ```sh
12	   ddx-agent-bench matrix \
13	     --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-canary.json \
14	     --harnesses=ddx-agent \
15	     --profiles=gpt-5-3-mini \
16	     --reps=3 \
17	     --out=benchmark-results/cost-observation-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
18	   ```
19	
20	2. Keep only the `git-leak-recovery` cell reports. For each report, record all
21	   four token streams:
22	
23	   - `input_tokens`
24	   - `output_tokens`
25	   - `cached_input_tokens`
26	   - `retried_input_tokens`
27	
28	3. Reconcile cost from the profile pricing source:
29	
30	   ```text
31	   cost_usd =
32	     input_tokens * input_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 +
33	     output_tokens * output_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 +
34	     cached_input_tokens * cached_input_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000
35	   ```
36	
37	   `retried_input_tokens` is tracked as an integrity signal. It is not billed
38	   separately unless the profile explicitly adds a future retried-input price.
39	
40	4. Derive caps:
41	
42	   ```text
43	   per_run_cap_usd = clamp(p95(observed_cost_usd) * 2.0, 1.00, 5.00)
44	   per_matrix_cap_usd = per_run_cap_usd * n_runs * 1.2
45	   ```
46	
47	5. Run the real matrix with both caps:
48	
49	   ```sh
50	   ddx-agent-bench matrix \
51	     --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-canary.json \
52	     --harnesses=ddx-agent,pi,opencode \
53	     --profiles=gpt-5-3-mini \
54	     --reps=3 \
55	     --per-run-budget-usd=<derived per-run cap> \
56	     --budget-usd=<derived matrix cap> \
57	     --out=benchmark-results/matrix-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
58	
59	   ddx-agent-bench matrix-aggregate benchmark-results/matrix-...
60	   ```
61	
62	   `costs.json` records the caps and every cell's token/cost totals.
63	
64	## Current Verification
65	
66	The repository-level automated verification uses the no-API `cost_probe`
67	adapter with the `smoke` profile. It emits deterministic token streams and a
68	positive synthetic cost. The matrix runner marks each over-budget run as
69	`process_outcome=budget_halted`, persists `final_status=budget_halted`, and
70	continues to later tuples.
71	
72	Live observation requires an API key and operator budget. Do not fabricate live
73	cost observations; commit the resulting matrix output directory path and cap
74	derivation only after the paid observation run has completed.

# Fizeau

Embeddable Go agent runtime - local-model-first via LM Studio.

[![CI](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Fizeau is a Go library that implements a coding agent runtime - a tool-calling
LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
Prioritizes local model inference via LM Studio and Ollama, with transparent
escalation to cloud providers.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/master/install.sh | bash
```
